claim: rumqttc's eventloop reconnects automatically after connection errors but does NOT re-establish subscriptions after reconnect — with clean sessions the client receives no further data from subscribed topics until it manually re-subscribes.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's rumqttc-based MQTT layer must explicitly re-subscribe on every reconnect; the library will not do it
scope_conditions: rumqttc, clean session / session_present=false, observed with keep_alive 5s and network-cable removal
quoted_support: rumqttc seems to recover/reconnect properly after connection error, but after the reconnect, I'm not seeing any data coming in from subscribed topics: ... Incoming = ConnAck(ConnAck { session_present: false, code: Success }) ... no more incoming data...
time_period: issue opened Feb 2021, still open Sept 2026, labelled in-pipeline

claim: The documented workaround for rumqttc losing subscriptions on reconnect is to call client.subscribe() again in the Err branch of the eventloop.poll() loop.
stance_target: agent reconnect handler design: re-subscribe in the poll error branch
quoted_support: Err(e) => { println!("Error = {:?}", e); // XXX: Here I have to re-subscribe to the topics :( client.subscribe("#", QoS::AtMostOnce).await.unwrap(); }

claim: rumqttc buffers and replays pending messages across broker outages (good), but provides no disconnect event/callback and no TTL or garbage collection for pending messages, so arbitrarily stale messages can be published on reconnect.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must bound stale telemetry age itself (timestamp check or queue cap), cannot rely on rumqttc
scope_conditions: rumqttc 0.2.0 era, issue still open and labelled stale/blocked
quoted_support: I can intercept ConnAck messages that means my app just reconnected to the broker, but is there any way to determine that it disconnected? ... Is there any way to specify a TTL when publishing messages or periodically "garbage collect" pending messages?
time_period: issue opened Dec 2020, still open Sept 2026

claim: rumqttc 0.25.1 advertises automatic reconnection by continuing the eventloop.poll() loop, client-side half-open connection detection via keep-alive pings, queue-size flow control, and natural backpressure during bad network — but outgoing packet throttling remains a TODO and only 35% of the crate is documented.
stance_target: assessing rumqttc fitness as the agent's MQTT client
quoted_support: Automatic reconnections by just continuing the eventloop.poll()/connection.iter() loop ... Natural backpressure to client APIs during bad network ... Throttling of outgoing packets (todo)

claim: In rumqttc's EventLoop::poll(), when select() returns an error the eventloop calls clean() which moves unacknowledged packets from state into a pending VecDeque for republication in the next session, and continuing to poll reconnects to the broker.
stance_target: the agent's poll loop must never exit on error — the loop itself IS the reconnect mechanism
quoted_support: Yields Next notification or outgoing request and periodically pings the broker. Continuing to poll will reconnect to the broker if there is a disconnection. **NOTE** Don't block this while iterating

claim: On reconnect, if the broker's ConnAck reports session_present=false, rumqttc clears ALL pending packets — queued messages are discarded unless a persistent session is negotiated.
stance_target: agent must use persistent sessions (clean_session=false / MQTT5 session expiry) if telemetry continuity across reconnects matters
scope_conditions: rumqttc main branch, MQTT v4 packets

claim: rumqttc's own eventloop source recommends setting AsyncClient's channel capacity to 0 (fully bounded) to manage the pending list length, and its flow control uses an inflight window with packet-id collision handling that pauses new outgoing requests until acks resolve.
stance_target: agent client configuration: bounded channel + awareness that collisions pause publishing
quoted_support: Also, while this helps prevent data loss, the pending list length should be managed properly. For this reason we recommend setting [`AsycClient`](crate::AsyncClient)'s channel capacity to `0`.

claim: There is no re-subscription logic anywhere in rumqttc's eventloop.rs; subscriptions live only in broker-side session state, so with clean sessions every reconnect loses all subscriptions.
stance_target: confirms issue #250 at the source level: re-subscribe responsibility is the caller's
scope_conditions: source audit of eventloop.rs at main
quoted_support: No re-subscription logic anywhere in eventloop.rs — subscriptions live in MqttState only via broker-side session; with clean sessions they are lost on every reconnect.
